title: Loop Counters, Boundaries and Off-by-One Errors
learningObjectives: Explain loop counters, boundaries and off-by-one errors and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: Loop bounds determine iteration count. For an N-element array, indexes are 0..N-1. Strict and inclusive comparisons change the final pass.
understand.whyItMatters: Boundary errors can skip the final item or access beyond valid memory.
understand.explain: Trace first and last values. Compare the loop condition to the valid index range.

examples.title: Valid array indexes
examples.explanation: Indexes are 0, 1, and 2; index 3 would be out of range.

examples.title: Trace increments by two
examples.explanation: Outputs 2, 4, 6; then i is 8 and condition fails.

examples.title: Container bound
examples.explanation: Use size() with strict less-than; use range-based for when no index is needed.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five Loop Counters, Boundaries and Off-by-One Errors examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating loop counters, boundaries and off-by-one errors in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: For N elements, last index is N-1.
Prefer i < size for index traversal.
Count passes separately from index values.
Test the first and last valid elements.
Avoid dereferencing or indexing past the end.

questions.explanation: Zero-based last index equals size minus one.
Index size is one past valid range.
